A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, table and Appendices A–I support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 and Appendix G report original diffusion-model experiments on Swiss Roll, MNIST and CIFAR10, plus VAE experiments on MNIST.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix G retain these original experiments, including bound estimates, test losses and generated samples.

M1.justification: The model architectures, training objectives, regularization suggestions and sampling procedures are retained. Appendix C.1.1 changes the mathematical representation used in the proof, without reporting an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VAEs on MNIST and diffusion models on Swiss Roll, MNIST and CIFAR10, including the same few-shot and full-data scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 4(a) retains the previous PAC-Bayes bound as comparator, and Figure 4(b) retains the memorization-score comparison. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendix G retain the training budgets, sample counts, preprocessing and KL/BPD estimation procedures. The fixed N = 1000 and fixed step size 0.001 comparisons already appear in v1.

E4.justification: The sample-size and diffusion-time sweeps, memorization analysis, generated-sample comparisons and Figure 7 discretization analysis are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five Monte Carlo training-dataset draws with different random seeds and retain the same uncertainty displays. The added expectations in theoretical bounds do not change empirical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figures 2–10 retain the same curves and generated examples. Reported findings are unchanged, including optimal diffusion times around 0.4–0.6 for Swiss Roll and 0.8 for the few-shot image experiments.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 replaces expectations over Xi with expectations over the full training set S. Corollaries 4.2–4.3 and Theorems 5.1 and 6.2 now bound expected divergence over S. Appendix C revises the marginalization over S−i and a KL-decomposition step, while new C.1.1 introduces a distribution-valued decoder output to define a fixed likelihood loss. These substantively revise central guarantees and their mathematical justification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a unified information-theoretic framework, improved VAE analysis, a diffusion-time trade-off and computable bounds using training data.

C2.justification: The revised formulas qualify the divergence guarantees as averages over training sets. Appendix C.1.1 newly explains why decoder-dependent likelihood loss requires different formal treatment from distance loss. Experimental interpretations and Appendix H limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains the same implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware information and code-access statement. No additional reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix I and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. The mathematical corrections do not introduce a new novelty claim or comparison with prior research.

P1.justification: Appendix C gains subsection C.1.1 and expanded explanations of training-set dependence and loss construction. Other proof prose receives localized edits; the main narrative and overall section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Expanded equation blocks and the new subsection reflow Appendices C–D, including regrouping the two corollary proofs on one page. Figures 1–10 and Table 1 retain their content, design and captions.

improvement.justification: Adding training-set expectations corrects the mismatch between the averaged generalization gap and v1's unaveraged divergence bounds. Appendix C also makes training-data dependence more explicit, improving precision and checkability. The gain remains limited: the new distribution-valued likelihood construction is not reconciled with the unchanged sampled-output information bound in Theorem 6.3, so a complete theoretical repair is not established.
